name: Rune-Inscribed Tablet
summary: In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives young Darkspear troll shamans a stone message. It sends promising mystics to Shikrik to begin formal communion with the elements.

sections.title: A Summons to the Spirits
sections.body: Gornek gives the rune-carved stone to initiates who prove their mettle in the Valley of Trials. The troll shaman Ishi-yo sent it to direct them to Shikrik, the shaman trainer. For Darkspear trolls, the tablet begins a shared path with the orcs, joining their old spiritual traditions with the shamanic heritage Warchief Thrall has renewed.

faq.q: What is the Rune-Inscribed Tablet used for?
faq.answer: Gornek gives the tablet to young troll shamans in the Valley of Trials. It directs them to Shikrik to begin their formal spiritual education.
The troll shaman Ishi-yo sends the tablet. It directs the initiate to Shikrik, the orc shaman trainer just outside the Den in the Valley of Trials, who knows they are coming.
Gornek gives this tablet to newly arrived Darkspear troll shamans as their initial class summons in Durotar.

angles.text: As a shaman, the tablet marks your first official step toward mastering earth, fire, water, and air. It reminds you that your strength flows from ancestral spirits.
As a Darkspear troll, you answer an orc trainer's summons, a sign of the growing bond and shared spiritual path between your people and their new Horde allies.
